summary: Canada's Vanier scholarship has been folded into a single federal doctoral award, the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D). It pays $40,000 a year for three years, and applicants of any citizenship can compete — provided they are already registered in a doctoral programme at a Canadian university.
covers: $40,000 (Canadian dollars) a year for three years.
Awarded by Canada's three research funding agencies — CIHR (health), NSERC (natural sciences and engineering) and SSHRC (social sciences and humanities).
It replaces both the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship ($50,000) and the former CGS-D ($35,000).
eligibility: International students who are registered in a doctoral programme at an eligible Canadian institution at the time of application.
Each agency and each university has a quota of applications it can put forward, so internal competition comes first.
Canadian citizens and permanent residents are also eligible.
how_to_apply: First, be admitted to and enrolled in a PhD at a Canadian university — this award does not fund applicants from abroad.
Apply through your university, which runs an internal competition and forwards its strongest candidates to the relevant agency.
University deadlines fall in September and October (for 2026: UBC 15 September, Waterloo 22 September, Dalhousie 5 October).
Prepare a research proposal, CV, transcripts and referee assessments as your university instructs.
watch_out: Vanier no longer exists — its last competition closed in autumn 2024. Sites still advertising Vanier are out of date.
The value dropped from $50,000 to $40,000 a year under the new programme.
Plan to apply in your first or second year of a Canadian PhD; you cannot use it to get there.
